topic.angle: A war-ending peace and the debate over its legacy

body.claim: The Peace of Westphalia ended the Thirty Years' War, which killed between 4.5 and 8 million people.
body.why: Two treaties signed in October 1648, in Osnabrück and Munster, brought peace to the Holy Roman Empire. They gave legal recognition to Calvinism alongside Catholicism and Lutheranism. Several scholars of international relations see the peace as the origin of principles crucial to modern international relations, known as Westphalian sovereignty. Some historians argue that this view only grew later, in the 19th and 20th centuries.

probes.question: What do some historians argue about 'Westphalian sovereignty'?
options: The idea of sovereignty it stands for emerged later, in the 19th and 20th centuries
